data.description:
AMSTERDAM, Nov. 20, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- New Amsterdam Invest N.V. a commercial real estate company listed on Euronext Amsterdam, confirms the closing of the transaction announced on 6 November 2026. The acquisition of 100% of the partnership interests in Tamiami Investments 2 Ltd has now been realized.

Tamiami Investments 2 Ltd. is a limited partnership that owns commercial real estate located at 12550 Professional Park Drive, 12600, 12601 & 12621 Corporate Lakes Drive, Fort Myers, Lee County, FL 33913, USA. Closing of the acquisition was expected to occur later in November 2026. Because of the closing, NAI now indirectly owns 100% of Tamiami Investments 2 Ltd. and, hence, indirectly 100% of said commercial real estate. With this acquisition NAI added a ninth property to its existing properties. This acquisition is fully aligned with NAI's business objectives and strategy.

For further details of this transaction reference is made to the press release of 6 November 2026.

About New Amsterdam Invest

New Amsterdam Invest N.V. is a commercial real estate company listed at Euronext Amsterdam with operating companies in the United States and the United Kingdom.

The main objective of New Amsterdam Invest is conducting commercial real-estate activities, including the owning, re-developing, acquiring, divesting, maintaining, letting out and/or otherwise operating commercial real estate, all in the broadest possible sense.

All information about New Amsterdam Invest can be found on the company website: www.newamsterdaminvest.com

data.title: COMBINED GENERAL MEETING OF NOVEMBER 20, 2026: ARGAN SHAREHOLDERS APPROVE THE MERGER WITH WDP
data.description:
Press release – Neuilly-sur-Seine, Friday, November 20, 2026 – 5.45 pm

COMBINED GENERAL MEETING OF NOVEMBER 20, 2026: ARGAN SHAREHOLDERS APPROVE THE MERGER WITH WDP

  • Approval of the cross-border merger by absorption of ARGAN into WDP, expected to be completed in the first quarter of 2027
  • Approval of the exceptional distribution of €11 per share, to be paid before completion of the merger
  • Progress on the conditions precedent

At the Combined General Meeting held on Friday, November 20, 2026, at the Palais Brongniart in Paris, ARGAN shareholders approved all resolutions supported by the Management Board and the Supervisory Board, paving the way for the merger with WDP.

As of the date of the meeting, ARGAN's share capital consisted of 25,766,939 shares, representing 25,748,892 voting rights. Shareholders present, represented, having granted a proxy to the Chairman or having voted by correspondence together held 22,429,229 shares and an equal number of voting rights, representing 87.10% of the total.

Approval of all resolutions supported by ARGAN's Management Board and Supervisory Board

The Combined General Meeting approved all resolutions supported by the Supervisory Board and the Management Board, including:

  • Resolution No. 3 approving the common draft terms of the cross-border merger entered into on July 23, 2026, between ARGAN and Warehouses De Pauw NV (“WDP”), as well as the merger by absorption of ARGAN into WDP (the “Merger”), adopted with 93.11% of the votes.

Under the terms of the common draft terms of the cross-border merger, each ARGAN share will be exchanged for 3 newly issued WDP shares. Completion of the Merger, which will result in the delisting of ARGAN shares from Euronext Paris and the admission to trading of the newly issued WDP shares on Euronext Brussels, Euronext Amsterdam and Euronext Paris, is expected to take place during the first quarter of 2027, subject to the satisfaction of the remaining conditions precedent. WDP's Extraordinary General Meeting, which will be called upon to approve the Merger, will be held on November 24, 2026.

  • Resolution No. 2 approving an exceptional distribution of €11 per share, to be paid out of share premium reserves (the “Exceptional Distribution”), adopted with 97.02% of the votes.

The ex-date and payment date of the Exceptional Distribution will be determined at a later date by the Management Board and announced in a press release. The Exceptional Distribution will take place before completion of the Merger.

Progress on the conditions precedent

In addition to the approval of the Merger by ARGAN's General Meeting, the following regulatory approvals required for completion of the Merger have recently been obtained. In particular:

  • The French Directorate General of Public Finances (Direction générale des finances publiques) issued a favourable tax ruling in line with the requests submitted by ARGAN and WDP;
  • The French Financial Markets Authority (Autorité des Marchés Financiers, ‘AMF’) confirmed that the transaction would not trigger a mandatory public buyout offer;
  • The Merger was approved by the relevant authorities under applicable foreign investment control regulations;
  • The Belgian Financial Services and Markets Authority (FSMA) approved the amendments to WDP's articles of association in connection with the Merger; and
  • The applicable waiting period for the European Commission's review of the Merger under the Foreign Subsidies Regulation has expired.

Completion of the Merger, which is expected to take place during the first quarter of 2027, remains subject to the other conditions precedent set out in Article 4 of the common draft terms of the cross-border merger, in particular the approval of the Merger by WDP's Extraordinary General Meeting, which will be held on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, and the issuance of the pre-merger certificates in France and Belgium.

Further information on the Merger is available on the Company's website and at www.wdp-argan.eu.

The full minutes of the General Meeting held on November 20, 2026, will be available on the Company's website by the end of the day. A replay of the General Meeting is available on argan.fr via the following link: https://argan.engagestream.euronext.com/assemblee_generale_extraordinaire_2026.

data.title: Markets were overdue for a tech correction, but trade will bounce – JPMorgan’s David Kelly
data.description:
The stock market was overdue for a tech correction, according to David Kelly, JPMorgan Asset Management's chief global strategist, who pointed to Nvidia's recent problems and broader technological disruptions as key factors driving the pullback.

In an interview with CNBC, Kelly noted that the troubles have been "rattling a few people."

Despite concerns about the AI trade and slowing demand in the tech sector , , Kelly sees inflation pressures easing and little evidence of broad economic overheating.

He expects falling gasoline prices (XB1:COM) alone will reduce the year-over-year increase in CPI by four-tenths of a percent for November.

"I see no evidence that in the big, broad economy outside of tech, there's that strong demand," Kelly said, pointing to flat new housing activity and weak consumer basics.

On Federal Reserve policy, Kelly pushed back against expectations for aggressive rate hikes. He characterized Fed Governor Waller as "a lonesome poke" in his support for a 50-basis-point hike, saying he does not believe the majority of Federal Reserve officials share that view.

Kelly anticipates a move in December followed by a pause rather than continued tightening.

He also argued that markets are constructing a hawkish Fed narrative in the absence of forward guidance, but he sees no justification for aggressive action.

"With rates already as pretty close to neutral levels, there's no reason for the Federal Reserve to be aggressive here," he said.

Looking ahead, Kelly expressed optimism about market resilience. He noted that steady inflows through 401(k) contributions, stock buybacks, and purchases by wealthy Americans provide consistent support.

"Unless you have a big reason for negativity, chances are this market will bounce," he said.

data.title: Kansas City Fed Services Activity Index Falls in November
data.description:
By Colin Kellaher

Services activity in the middle of the U.S. slowed in November, while expectations for future activity moved higher, according to a monthly survey by the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City.

The Tenth District Services Survey's composite index, a weighted average of indexes covering revenue/sales, employment and inventory, came in at 3 in November, down from 10 in October but up from 0 in September. Readings above zero indicate expansion, while those below zero indicate contraction.

The Kansas City Fed said growth eased in both business and consumer services, driven by modest declines in auto and real-estate services.

The bank said its index of expectations for future services activity came in at 20 in November, up from 4 in October.

The Kansas City Fed's survey, released Friday, includes participants from such service industries as retail and wholesale trade, automobile dealers, real estate and restaurants. The survey provides information on current services activity in the Tenth District, which includes Colorado, Oklahoma, Wyoming, Nebraska, Kansas, the northern half of New Mexico and the western third of Missouri.

The bank's monthly manufacturing survey, released Thursday, showed that factory activity in the central U.S. rose in November.

Soros Fund, led by George Soros, also trimmed its position, lowering its holdings from approximately 190,000 shares to 122,000 shares.

The full exit represents one of the more notable institutional departures from the stock during Q3. Corvex Management, led by Keith Meister, also exited its 132,000-share position entirely.

data.title: ICE Canola Holding to Up One Day, Down the Next Pattern
data.description:

The rangebound Canadian oilseed was on course to hold true to its pattern this week of up one day and down the next.

"We need fresh demand at these levels," a trader said, noting that export buyers haven't stepped up lately.

The trader also said the U.S. markets "are soft and volatile." He added that if crude oil prices would stabilize, that would lead to stability for canola and other vegetable oils.

Declines in crude oil were accelerating Friday, putting greater pressure on the veg oils. That weighed on Chicago soyoil, European rapeseed and Malaysian palm oil. However, Chicago soybeans and soymeal were still on the rise.

The forecast for canola ending stocks in 2026-27 were trimmed by 100,000 metric tons by Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada in its November supply and demand report. AAFC now expects the carryout to be 1.87 million metric tons, versus 1.89 million in 2025-26.

Shares of Savara slid after the Food and Drug Administration said it would miss its own target action date for a license of the biopharmaceutical company's rare lung disease treatment.

data.title: A Miami Honeymoon Inspired One Couple to Build a Candy-Colored Home in London — WSJ
data.description:
By Ruth Bloomfield

Inspired by Miami's Art Deco architecture, the eccentric but charming Cloud House in north London took architect Peter Morris and his wife, Emily Kennedy, a decade to create.

With its marshmallow-pink exterior, turquoise-framed windows and the fluted roofline that inspired its name, the house cost them about $971,000 to build — nearly as much as the roughly $1.25 million that the couple had paid for the site in 2016.

Now, less than three months after moving in, the couple are listing the approximately 1,404-square-foot house in the neighborhood of Gospel Oak for GBP2.5 million, or about $3.3 million.

Morris, founder of Peter Morris Architects, and Kennedy, a television producer, are selling because they want a new house-building challenge, said Kennedy, who had renovated a half-dozen houses before Cloud House. "We knew we would not stay here forever," she said. "But it was beautiful to make this dream house."

The property initially came with a two-bedroom Victorian cottage and a backyard to the side, which Morris said he saw potential to redevelop.

The couple got married in 2017 and spent their honeymoon in Miami. "It was inspiring — all the beautiful curves on the buildings," said Morris. "The colors, the turquoise sea and the pink flamingos."

As soon as Morris returned to London, with Kennedy's encouragement, he started drawing up plans to replace the cottage with a pair of three-story houses.

It took the couple four years to persuade local planners to let them proceed with their unusual vision. To help finance the property, the couple listed one of the houses as a work-in-progress, offering the land, the plans and Morris's assistance in getting it built. A young East London-based family paid roughly $1.32 million for it. They will be moving in before Christmas.

Work finally began in 2023 with the demolition of the cottage. The design of the house was also inspired by other playful spaces, including traditional sweet shops, ice cream parlors and fairgrounds, Morris said.

The commitment to this theme goes beyond the exterior. The kitchen island is pink with green-and-white cabinet doors and yellow handles. Sections of the kitchen ceiling are candy-striped in pink and white, with beaded cornicing. The floor is mint green, and the doors leading to Morris's study, a guest bathroom and the staircase are cobalt blue.

Upstairs, the couple obliged the request of their 20-year-old daughter, Astha Morris, a college student who wanted a pink-and-red bathroom beside her bedroom.

One of the couple's favorite features is the roof terrace, enclosed by pink plaster walls. With views of a nearby Victorian church spire and neighboring buildings, it is fitted with a tub and seating.

The property has attracted so much attention that it was featured on the British TV series "Grand Designs," with presenter Kevin McCloud describing it as "one perfectly baked pink pudding."

For listing agent Becky Fatemi of United Kingdom Sotheby's International Realty, valuing the house was a challenge, but she said it commands a premium for the neighborhood, despite its relatively modest floor space. "You can look at all the comparables in Gospel Oak, but none of them will tell you what Cloud House is worth," she said.

data.title: Tech stocks tumble, Treasury yields fall as traders seek refuge
data.description:
Key points:
  • Ex-Japan Asian stocks post biggest weekly drop since COVID hit
  • Anthropic shares fall as much as 12.5%
  • US bonds rally, gold and silver at 2026 lows

By Rodrigo Campos and Harry Robertson

Tumbling technology-related shares led a global stock selloff on Friday, with US traders rotating into defensive sectors and the US 10-year yield dropping by the most in a month.

Stock benchmarks in Japan and Korea tumbled over 5% overnight to close the week, while on Wall Street chipmaker shares were down close to 6%. Taiwanese shares TWSE:TAIEX were down 17% for the week, their biggest weekly decline since 1990. Anthropic fell as much as 12.5% on its first full day of trading.

Consumer staples and healthcare led sector gains on the S&P 500, which was still on track to post its largest weekly loss since March 2025.

"Markets are entering a more defensive phase," said Daniela Hathorn, senior market analyst at Capital.com.

"Strong AI demand and successful individual listings are no longer sufficient to sustain broader risk appetite when investors are questioning valuations, borrowing costs and the outlook for corporate profitability."

The Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.08% to 49,135.56, the S&P 500 CBOE:SPX fell 1.20% to 7,089.64 and the Nasdaq Composite fell 2.37% to 23,314.06.

MSCI's gauge of stocks across the globe EURONEXT:IACWI fell 1.60% and the pan-European STOXX 600 index fell 1.83%. Emerging market stocks CBOE:EFS fell 3.11%.

The MSCI index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan (.MISX00000PUS) tumbled 8.3% this week, its largest such drop since the COVID pandemic in March 2020.

The VIX index, linked to the cost of insurance against a drop on the S&P 500, traded at its highest since March .

As investors sought safe-haven assets, government bonds rallied.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year notes fell 10.43 basis points to 4.948% and the 30-year bond (US30YT=RR) yield fell 6.39 basis points to 5.3371%. The 10-year yield is on track to post its largest daily basis point drop since October 22.

The 2-year note (US2YT=RR) yield, which typically moves in step with interest rate expectations for the Federal Reserve, fell 12.57 basis points to 4.653% even as a rate hike is priced in for next month's policy meeting.

DOLLAR AND OIL DROP

The dollar index dipped after touching a 19-month high on Thursday. The dollar's recent rally has been fueled by bets on tighter monetary policy due to hotter-than-expected US inflation data.

"I think the momentum has stalled for the dollar ... but I think it's a little bit early to pick a top for the dollar," said Marc Chandler, chief market strategist at Bannockburn Capital Markets.

The dollar index fell 0.21% to 103.73, with the euro up 0.15% at $1.0982. Against the Japanese yen , the dollar weakened 0.62% to 158.7.

In commodities, crude prices fell on strong exports from the Middle East and reports of tanker disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.

US crude fell 0.75% to $82.59 a barrel and Brent fell to $91.02 per barrel, down 1.04% on the day.

Spot gold fell 2.02% to $3,548.53 an ounce and spot silver fell 2.54% to $41.66 an ounce, both trading at their lowest since September 2025. Copper declined 2.71% to $12,186.00 a ton.
